To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
defaunation of the rumen reduced nutrient digestion, but supplementation with either sodium bicarbonate or urea increased nutrient digestion.

(1) Defaunation decreased nutrient digestibilities in sheep; (2) Urea supplementation increased digestibility of nutrients in defaunated and faunated sheep; (3) Sodium bicarbonate supplementation decreased ruminal pH, increased ruminal fluid isovalerate concentration and total tract digestibility of ADF and CP in defaunated, but not faunated, sheep.
defaunation of the rumen reduced the digestion of fiber and increased the flow of fatty acids into the duodenum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of urea or NaHCO3 supplementation to a high-fiber diet on nutrient digestion and characteristics of the defaunated sheep rumen.

the effects of defaunation on ruminal and intestinal digestion and the effects of urea, sodium bicarbonate, or a combination of the two on ruminal characteristics of the defaunated sheep fed a high-fiber diet.
the development of a new technology for the treatment of wastewater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of urea or bicarbonate supplementation on the nutrient digestibility and ruminal fermentation in defaunated or faunated sheep are dependent on several factors including the diet composition and the level and form of the supplemental urea and bicarbonate.
the addition of urea or/and sodium bicarbonate in a high-fiber diet fed to defaunated sheep increased the nutrient digestion and rumen pH.

urea and sodium bi-carbonate supplementation increased nutrient digestion by the defaunated sheep and urea supplementation increased nutrient digestion and decreased ruminal fluid isovalerate concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of sodium bicarbonate to a high-fiber diet increased nutrient digestibility in defaunated and faunated sheep.
urea and sodium supplementation increased nutrient digestion and decreased ruminal fluid isopropanol and ammonia concentrations.
defaunation of the rumen decreased the efficiency of utilization of nutrients from the diet and that urea and sodium carbonate supplementation increased nutrient digestibility in defaunated animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
urea and sodium carbonate supplementation can improve nutrient digestion in defaunated ruminants.
defaunation can be used to reduce methane production without reducing nutrient digestibility.
the addition of urea and/or sodium bicarbonate to the diet of defaunated animals can improve nutrient digestion and reduce ruminal acidosis.
